J5. Selection of measuring section and conditions of installation The layout of transducer locations and measurement of as-built dimensions must be done using a~cunte methods. For large conduits surveying techniques and for smaller conduits careful shop measurements can be used. In either case the uncertainties of the as-built measurements must be accounted for in the error analysis (see Clause J7). Special cart shall bc taken for large conduits which may not have perfectly symmetrical shapes. A representative dimension D shall be determined in the measuring section and perpendicular to the direction of the acoustic paths. At least five equally spaced measurements of D shall be taken (see Figure J3) including one at the centrc of the measuring section and one at each end. These measurements shall be avcragcd to bc representative of the conduit dimension, in the measuring section.

Measurement planes

Figure J3 - Locations for measurements of D A sufficient number of other mcasuremcnts shall be taken to dctcrminc the shape of ihc conduit for purposes of dctcrmining the cffcct of the conduit shape on the numerical integration correction cocfficicnt k. Accurate mcasurcmcnls of as-built dimensions of D (and possibly I?) of the conduit, acoustic path bclwccn transducer facts. path lengths between the walls of the conduit along the acoustic paths and the location of the acoustic paths and their angles relative to the ccntrc of the conduit &arc to-bc used in the calculalion of lhc.disch,argc.
lcnglhs

Misplaccmcnts of transducer locations must be accounted for in the error analysis or by correction to the calculated discharge. As distortion of the velocity prolilc may be caused by a bend, the intersection of the two acoustic plants should bc in the plane of the bend to minimize the effects of the transverse flow components on the accuracy of the measurement. Individual measurements of velocity 5 shall be made for each pathin order to obtain an indication of any distortion in the velocity profile and the extent of any transverse flow components.

208

IS/IEC 41( 1991)

Although lhc USC of two four-path plants compensates for most of the transverse vclocily components, the measuring section should be chosen as far as possible from any upstream disturbances, such as a bend, that could crcatc asymmetry of the velocity distribution, swirl or large scale turbulence. Other factors that may product transverse velocity components or distortion of the velocity protile arc flow conditions upstream of the intake, the shape of the intake, the number of bends upstream of the measuring section, changes in upstream conduit diameter and the proximity of bends or changes in conduit diameter downstream. It is rccommcndcd that there should bc a straight length of upstream conduit bctwecn the measuring section and any important irrcgukarity of at least ten conduit diameters. Similarly,thcrc should bc a straight length of at lcast three conduit diamctcrs bctwecn the measuring section and any important downstream irregularity. Expcricncc has shown that satisfactory results can bc obtained with a single four path acoustic plant located downstream of a straight length of twenty conduit diameters or more providing a uniform llow distribution in the measuring scetion. Measurement of discharge. using a single path in one or two measuring planes is not permitted under the rules of this standard. Provision in the design and construction of the flow ~metermust bs made for demonstrating that the cquipmcnt is operating correctly. It shall bc possible to make such checks as:
-

showing acoustic pulses and their dctcction on an oscilloscope; internal clcctronic tests of the program and constants;

-

- comparison of calculated values of the speed of sound using the measured acoustic path transit times and path lengths with published values corrcctcd for water tempcraturc; scparatc mcasurcmcnt of the avcragc velocity along each individual path.

It may bc dcsirablc to measure the acoustic pulse transit times indcpcndcntly and compare with the results given by the mcasurcmcnt system.
J6. Conditions of-use

and limitation~s

Flow v&city and diamctcr of the conduit shall bc large enough to permit an accurate &termination of the diffcrcncc in acoustic pulse transit times taking into account the accuracy of the timer. Measurements with flow velocities less than 1.5 m/s and diameters of conduits less than 0,8 m should bc avoided. Bubbles, sediment and acoustic noise may disrupt the operation of the acoustic flow measurement system and should be avoided. If the disruption results in missed samples, enough valid samples must bc obtained to be compatible with the assumptions used in the error analysis. The design of the data acquisition and trcatmcnt system shall permit checking of the proportion~of lost pulses.

IS/IEC

41 ( 1991)

37. Uncertainty

of measurement

Both random and systcmalic unccrlaintics have to bc taken into account. For a dctailcd analysis, see IS0 5168. Specifically, the following sources of uncertainty have been idcntificd: mcasurcmcnt of path lcnglhs L and L,,; mcasurcmcnt of acoustic path angles v; mcasurcmcnt of path spacing cland conformity with the positions prcscribcd; mcasurcmcnt of D; time mcasurcmcnt and time resolution; non-water path time estimation; internal computational precision; uncertainty due to flow distortion around the transducers; existcncc of transvcrsc flow components;
flow profile

distortions;

spatial variations of speed of sound; spatial variations of flow-vclocily along the conduit; variations of flow vclccity, speed of sound and discharge with time.

The first eight items listed are usually combined into an overall instrument uncertainty. This uncertainty is in most cases cstimatcd to bc less than rtO,5 %. The next four items arc associated with the flow field and its trcatmcnt and may result in a correction factor and possibly an additional systematic uncertainty. This systcmalic uncertainty shall bc combined with the instrument uncertainty in a root mean square relationship to product an overall systematic uncertainly. The last item associated with the time variations of flow velocity and speed of sound results in a random uncertainty. Limited cxpcricncc with the USC of lhis method does not permit the rcliablc asscssmcnt of a gcncrally applicable systematic uncertainty. In gcncral, the use of a two-plane mctcr will likely rcducc the overall systematic uncertainty which might bc assumed as being of the same order of magnitude as for currcntmclcrs used in the same conditions, i.c. bctwecn fl, 0 % and f2,O %.
